Mohd Altaf Age 45 Years vs Union Territory Of Jammu And
Kashmir on 2 April, 2024 
Author: Sanjeev Kumar
Bench: Sanjeev Kumar
 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Jammu
 ...
 Hcp No. 68/2023
 Reserved on: 07.03.2024
 Pronounced on:02.04.2024
Mohd Altaf Age 45 years
S/o Mohd. Iqbal
Through his wife Khalida Kouser Age 40 years
R/O Gadyog, Tehsil Khawas
Rajouri. ......Petitioner(s)
 Through: Mr. Ayushman Kotwal, Advocate. 
 Vs.
 1. Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,
 Through Secretary
 Home Department,
 Civil Secretariat Jammu/ Srinagar.
 2. District Magistrate Rajouri.
 3. Sr. Superintendent of Police Rajouri. 
 4. Superintendent District Jail, Dhangiri, Rajouri. 
 . .....Respondent(s)
 Through: Mr. Bhanu Jasrotia, Ga.
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice Sanjeev Kumar, Judge
 Judgement 
1.  The petitioner is aggrieved and has challenged his detention ordered by the respondent No.2 vide Order No. DMR/Index/17 of 2023 dated 28-07-2023, whereby the petitioner has been placed under preventive detention with a view to prevent him from acting in any manner prejudicial to the security of the State. 
2. The subjective satisfaction drawn by respondent No.2 is founded on the grounds of detention prepared on the basis of dossier supplied by Senior Superintendent of Police, Rajouri, and served Mohd Altaf Age 45 Years vs Union Territory Of Jammu And Kashmir on 2 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131894743/
1 upon the detenue at the time of execution of the detention order.
3. The petitioner is shown to be instrumental in instigating the masses to create law and order problem being a strong motivator of Jihad as well as good orator with ability to attract large number of people, especially youth by his inflammatory and highly objectionable speeches. It is stated that the petitioner is an over ground worker of terrorist outfit and is closely associated with those organizations whose main aim is to create disruptive activities and spread separatist feelings in the minds of the people. The petitioner is involved in aiding and abetting terrorists and is found in indulging in antinational activities and has even been declared as Over Ground worker. It is also stated that the petitioner is also involved in FIR No. 31/2023 registered under Section 212 IPC at Police Station Budhal wherein the charge sheet has been presented before the competent Court of law. The petitioner had been providing food, shelter and basic information about the security forces to the terrorist outfits and is more dangerous than the terrorists as he is acting on the tune of the anti-national/ POK agencies who are bent upon to wage war against the sovereignty and integrity of the nation and his activities are highly prejudicial to the security of the State. 
4. The impugned order of detention is challenged by the petitioner primarily on the following grounds:-
(i) That the impugned order suffers from non-application of mind. The respondent No.2 has, in the order of detention, referred to alleged commission of various offences and registration of FIR, but has not spelled out the involvement of the petitioner in the commission of any activity which has the potential of being prejudicial to the security of the State. The respondent No.2 has thus failed to make a distinction between what is prejudicial to security of the State and what is only a problem of law and order;
(ii) That the petitioner was not provided with the requisite material relied upon by the respondent No.2 to draw subjective satisfaction as a result whereof the petitioner was deprived of his right to make an effective representation to the Government against his detention;
(iii) That the grounds of detention are vague and irrational and, therefore, vitiates the subjective satisfaction of the detaining authority.
5. Respondents have filed the counter affidavit of respondent No.2- District Magistrate. The plea of the petitioner is contested primarily on the ground that the consistent and persistent unlawful activities of the petitioner have given sense of insecurity to the people of the area and have the potential of endangering the human life, disturbing the public peace and tranquility so as to bring the activities of the petitioner within the sweep of public order. The respondents have also produced the original record to demonstrate that all the procedural requirements were duly followed while executing the order of detention. 
Mohd Altaf Age 45 Years vs Union Territory Of Jammu And Kashmir on 2 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131894743/
2 6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record, I am of the considered opinion that the grounds of detention, on the basis of which the petitioner has been put under preventive detention, are totally vague, uncertain and devoid of any material. The impugned order, passed on the basis of such grounds of detention, is, on the face of it, not sustainable in law and deserves to be quashed. 
7. From reading of grounds of detention it clearly transpires that the petitioner has been detained under Section 8 of the Public Safety Act, 1978, for his activities calculated to endanger the security of the State. There is reference to the petitioner making inflammatory and highly objectionable speeches and motivating the masses to choose the path of violence to create serious law and order problem in the District of Rajouri. There is no date, month or year indicated in the grounds of detention on which the petitioner allegedly made the inflammatory and objectionable speeches. It is also not forthcoming from the grounds of detention whether these inflammatory and objectionable speeches are with a view to over off the authority of the State or create any situation prejudicial to the security of the State. There is rather reference to the creation of law and order problem in the District of Rajouri by the youth who get inspired by such speeches. It is also interesting to note that despite the petitioner having been indulging in making inflammatory and highly objectionable speeches, has not been booked in any criminal case. The only FIR which is referred to in the grounds of detention is FIR No. 31/2023 registered under Section 212 IPC at Police Station Budhal. 
8. From the brief facts narrated in reference to the aforesaid FIR, it would transpire that even the offence under Section 212 IPC is not prima facie made against the petitioner. There are serious allegations of harboring the militants leveled against the petitioner but there is no mention as to the identity of a person who has been horboured or concealed by the petitioner with an intention of screening him from legal punishment. In the absence of any named offender who is allegedly harboured, it is prima facie not tenable to book a person for commission of offence punishable under Section 212 IPC. Without commenting upon the merits of the FIR, which will ultimately be subject to determination by the competent Court, suffice it to say that mere narration of activities,
without there being any iota of material in support thereof, cannot be said to be relevant material on the basis of which the detaining authority may derive its subjective satisfaction, which is sine qua non for placing a person under preventive detention. The grounds of detention are totally vague,
uncertain and in the nature of storytelling and, therefore, do not furnish requisite material required for making subjective satisfaction with regard to the necessity of placing the petitioner under preventive detention. There is nothing in the grounds of detention to suggest that why the petitioner, who is already booked in FIR No. 31/2023 under Section 212 IPC registered at Police Station Budhal, cannot be dealt with under the ordinary law. 
9. Otherwise also, from perusal of detention records produced by the respondents, it clearly transpires that the impugned order of detention was executed on 01-08-2023 and at the time of execution of the detention order the petitioner was only provided a copy of order of detention ( one leaf) and copy of grounds of detention (3 leafs). The petitioner was not provided any other material,
in particular copy of the FIR No. 31/2023 registered at Police Station Budhal. The other material like delivery of inflammatory speeches by the petitioner, which is though lacking material particulars, too has not been supplied to the petitioner. In this way the petitioner has been deprived Mohd Altaf Age 45 Years vs Union Territory Of Jammu And Kashmir on 2 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131894743/
3 of his fundamental right of making representation against his detention to the competent authority. 
In taking this view, I am supported by a judgment of Honble the Supreme Court delivered in Thahira Haris etc. v. Government of Karnataka, (2009) 11 SCC 438, wherein it has been held thus:-
"28. Our Constitution provides adequate safeguards under clauses (5) and (6) of Article 22 to the detenu who has been detained in pursuance of the order made under any law providing for preventive detention. He has right to be supplied copies of all documents, statements and other materials relied upon in the grounds of detention without any delay. The predominant object of communicating the grounds of detention is to enable the detenu at the earliest opportunity to make effective and meaningful representation against his detention."
10. For the foregoing reasons, I find merit in this petition and the same is, accordingly, allowed. The impugned order of detention is quashed with a direction to the respondents to release the detenue forthwith, if not required in any other case.
